_meta.purpose: Per-ARRIVAL disposition — which record was looked at, by whom, and where it went. Keyed by (channel, recordId) so a batch can never be cleared by one of its members. PUBLIC repo: never her words and never a transcript, only where the record went.
_meta.seeAlso: feedback-log.json holds the same lifecycle for the feedback channel.

baseline.why: This control was built 2026-08-28. Arrivals before it were governed by the channel watermark in .private/channel-read-state.json — a batch instrument. The baseline is therefore ITSELF a batch clear, declared once and dated rather than applied silently, and it is never reported as a disposition: those records are `baselined` (covered by the watermark, never individually attested), which is a different sentence from `we looked and it was Paul's`. The first run found 69 arrivals with no disposition of their own; 68 fall behind this line, and the 69th — the 2026-08-09 Fairway recording this whole control came out of — is dispositioned explicitly below. The count is printed on every clean run so a green tick can never hide it. Do NOT extend this date to quiet a finding.
baseline.declaredBy: paul-stated 2026-08-28 ('let's just go ahead and take care of this')

dispositioned.disposition: Paul's own bench test at the Fairway zone; disregard. Nothing to fold to canon.
dispositioned.attestedBy: Paul LISTENED to the audio, 2026-08-28 — a human ear, not a model read. Prior legs (2 model transcripts, deviceId, sibling observation 52s later) agreed but were all inference.
